Raw PE import parse: d3d11.dll IAT = 0xC37A50 holding only D3D11CreateDevice. Thunk 0xA3B968 decodes to VA 0x01037A50. Calls at 0x5BC3A0 and 0x5BC3EC in InitDevice. Import DLL list has no dxgi.dll and no other d3d entry; delay-import table holds only the two api-ms-win-gaming-tcui DLLs.

Cells 0xC370B0 (D3DPreprocess, call 0x5BE19E) and 0xC370B8 (D3DReflect, call 0x5B8F1A) confirmed from the raw import directory. Extra finding: if D3DPreprocess fails (r0<0 at 0x5BE1A2) the game does strb 0 to this+0x31 and silently abandons the stage (branch to 0x5BE986) WITHOUT reaching D3DCompile, so the host's D3DCompile failure log would never show include or preprocess errors. For bring-up it is worth hooking cell 0xC370B0 as a logging-only forwarder.

Independently decoded the call at 0x5BE4BA: r0=this+0x58 data (SSO test on this+0x6C), r1=[this+0x68], r2=source-name std::string data, r3=r7+0x1728, [sp]=r7+0x1590 (vptr 0x0176B164 stored at 0x5BDFDA), [sp+4]='main', [sp+8]=target string, [sp+0xc]=0x8000, [sp+0x10]=sb (only write to sb after entry is mov sb,#0 at 0x5BE2B8), [sp+0x14]=r7+0x1580, [sp+0x18]=r7+0x1578 => 11 arguments, same layout as the x86 hook. Target construction (0x5BE2E0..0x5BE3A2): FL 9_x -> major 4 minor 0 + _level_9_x suffix, 10_0 -> 4_0, 10_1 -> 4_1, 11_0/11_1 -> 5_0. Function start/bytes verified (2de9f04f0df11c0b43f692f140f20a64); callers 0x5BD3D0 (3 calls this+4/+8/+0xC, r1=this+0x20) and 0x4A1DF0 verified.

rtti HeaderInclude -> vtable 0x0136B164; slot0 VA 0x9BB181 -> RVA 0x5BB180 (bytes 2de9f04b0df1180b46f638f0adf26c4d match), slot1 -> 0x8B980 (12-byte return-0 stub). Open reads its stack args at [sp+0x490]/[sp+0x494] (0x48C frame + 4-byte prolog-helper push at 0x11FC), stores data ptr / size there, then moves the std::string into a vector at this+4 (sub_AB1F0) so the heap buffer outlives the call. Minor caveat the finder missed: for contents shorter than 16 bytes the std::string is SSO and *ppData points into Open's own dead stack frame (0x5BB26C..0x5BB27E); the host proxy calls HeaderInclude via Open then HeapAlloc before CopyMemory, so a tiny include could be clobbered (same latent hazard on x86/UWP; irrelevant for real shaders).

Literal 'tex.CalculateLevelOfDetailUnclamped(TextureSampler0, uv)' occurs exactly once in the package (data/shaders/hlsl/util.fxh:8; the 9 versioned data/shaders/<guid>/hlsl dirs do not contain it) and not in the exe (str search empty). Use of texture2D_AA is guarded by !TEXEL_AA || !TEXEL_AA_FEATURE || VERSION<0xa000. Additional info: TEXEL_AA_FEATURE is not static - the exe adds it as a define at 0x5C2128 only when a runtime capability byte ([[r6]+0x31] in sub_5C1F1C) is set, and the same function adds R8G8B8A8_SNORM_UNSUPPORTED via GameOwner::hasFeature (0x5BC524). So the intrinsic is only compiled on devices the game itself deems capable; 'probably unnecessary' is a reasonable recommendation but remains a hypothesis (cannot be proven statically; I could not confirm which shader profile minimum CalculateLevelOfDetailUnclamped needs for FL10_0/ps_4_0, so keep the proxy ready).
grep -rl 'ROOT_SIGNATURE|RootSignature' over the whole package data dir -> nothing; arm32re str RootSignature / ROOT_SIGNATURE -> nothing in the exe. Patch is a no-op on 1.2.8.

Both D3DPreprocess (0x5BE19E) and D3DCompile (0x5BE4BA) pass [sp]=r7+0x1590, the HeaderInclude object; no code path passes 0 or 1. Host win32_d3d_compile (win32_host.c 9623-9693) branch for D3D_COMPILE_STANDARD_FILE_INCLUDE is therefore dead.

InitDevice 0x5BC258 (pdata start, bytes 2de9f04f0df11c0b44f6ccf792b06f46 match): stack args [sp]=levels,[sp+4]=count,[sp+8]=7,[sp+0xC]=owner+0xC0,[sp+0x10]=owner+0xB8,[sp+0x14]=renderer+0x110; r0=[owner+0xC4], r1=driver type, r2=0, r3=flags. WARP retry at 0x5BC3EC with r1=5 reproduced. Precision fixes: (1) driver type is 1 (HARDWARE) in the normal path; it becomes 0 only when owner+0xBC!=0 AND owner+0xC4 (adapter) != 0 (cbz at 0x5BC302 skips the adapter test when +0xBC==0). (2) the game's own owner factory 0x13F2A0 explicitly sets owner+0xB8=0x9100, owner+0xBC=0, +0xC0/+0xC4=0 after the ctor, so owner+0xBC==0 -> flags=0 and 7-entry level list holds also on the game's path. The conclusions (keep 0x20 OR, drop Win7 11_1 filter, drop WARP retry, drop captured_* logic) stand.

Reproduced with different functions: ctor 0x5BB62C zeroes renderer+0x110..0x144; getContext 0x5BB8D8 loads +0x110; getDevice 0x5BB8AC loads renderer+0x108 then +0xC0; DiscardWindowViews 0x582970 uses +0x114/+0x118/+0x120; owner ctor 0x5B7E7C stores owner back-pointer at renderer+0x108 (str r4,[r3,#0x108] at 0x5B7F20) and renderer at owner+0xAC (0xAC confirmed also by 0x13DB5C releasing [owner+0xAC] with size 0x204 and owner size 0xD0).

VA 0x019B86AC = RVA 0x015B86AC (owner, 81 xrefs, created by 0x13DB5C/0x13F2A0, used by the VERSION macro path 0x5BDF18..0x5BDF24 and DiscardWindowViews) and VA 0x019B86B0 = RVA 0x015B86B0 confirmed. Resolved the finder's open question: the screen object's floats are WRITTEN by MinecraftGame::windowSizeChanged(this,w,h) (vf24, RVA 0x12F8F0, stores (float)w at +0x14, (float)h at +0x18 at 0x12F92C/0x12F930; note the quirk 'if sub_130f60() && 0x230<=h<=0x26C then h=0x244') and read by Renderer::createWindowSizeDependentResources 0x5BB774 (lround of +0x18/+0x14 -> Display::resizeSwapChain) and by setScissorRect. So the scissor height equals whatever the host passes to windowSizeChanged. Not a gfx_compat bug, but the porter must call windowSizeChanged with the HWND client size. Confidence stays medium only because sub_130f60's meaning is unresolved.

missing: install_swap_chain_present_hook / win32_present (win32_host.c 10024-10044, called at 11571): patches IDXGISwapChain vtable slot 8 (Present) of the host-created swap chain. It is architecture independent (4-byte slots, Thumb pointers) and reads no game struct, but it has no fact in gfx_compat (probably belongs to gfx_device/gfx_init); the ARM host just keeps it unchanged.

D3DPreprocess failure is silent (see iat_d3d_preprocess_reflect): game aborts the stage at 0x5BE1A2 and never calls D3DCompile, so the host's failure logging in win32_d3d_compile cannot see include/preprocess errors. Recommend a logging-only hook of cell 0xC370B0 (D3DPreprocess, 7 args: src r0,size r1,name r2,defines r3,include [sp],ppText [sp+4],ppErrors [sp+8]).

Shader-variant defines built outside compileShaderProgram: sub_5C1F1C (RVA 0x5C1F1C) adds TEXEL_AA_FEATURE and R8G8B8A8_SNORM_UNSUPPORTED etc. based on GameOwner::hasFeature (0x5BC524, reads owner+0xB8 feature level and other owner bytes). No x86 host dependency, but these game-side caps depend on InitDevice having filled owner+0xB8/+0xC0 and on queryAdapterInfo 0x5B9F4C having run (called from 0x134EB2 in the game's own init chain 0x134D40, which also calls ensure_owner_global_reset 0x13DB5C then InitDevice) - the gfx_init porter should replicate that order.

Owner creation difference: the game's own factory 0x13F2A0 does new 0xD0, memset, owner ctor 0x5B7E7C, then owner+0xB8=0x9100, +0xBC=0, +0xC0/+0xC4=0. The x86-style host path (ZeroMemory + ctor only) leaves +0xB8=0 until InitDevice succeeds; harmless, but the porter can instead call 0x13DB5C (creates owner and installs it into 0x015B86AC) as an alternative.

MinecraftGame::windowSizeChanged 0x12F8F0 writes the screen-object floats used by scissor and swap-chain resize (see owner_global_and_screen_global); no fact lists it as an x86 dependency of the scissor hook.

PE flag (outside this area, FYI): ARM exe DllCharacteristics=0x9140 includes IMAGE_DLLCHARACTERISTICS_APPCONTAINER (0x1000); the x86 'patched' exes presumably have it cleared, so the winmain/pe porter must handle it.

No missing x86 RVA constants: RVA_128_D3D_COMPILE_IAT, D3D11_CREATE_DEVICE_IAT, DXGI_DEVICE3_IID, D3D_CONTEXT_IID, D3D_ANNOTATION_IID, DISCARD_WINDOW_VIEWS, INIT_DEVICE, OWNER_GLOBAL and the renderer/owner offsets are all accounted for.
